question: Does the propagator coordinate that mattered in SMACS have a similar raw image-plane response in a second cluster at much higher lens redshift?

raw_data.source: Paterno-Mahler et al. 2018, ApJ 863 154, arXiv:1805.09834v2, multiple-image table
raw_data.included: Spectroscopic z=1.358 knot systems 1, 10, 11, and 12, plus secure z=4.013 images 3.1, 3.2, and 3.5.
raw_data.excluded: System 2 lacks a spectroscopic redshift; candidate images 3.3, 3.4, and 3.6 were excluded from the paper's preferred secure model.

evaluation.selection: Choose minimum calibration linearized image-plane RMS on SPT only; score held-out subfamilies without refitting p, fraction, or amplitude.
evaluation.SMACS_locked_control: Also score p=1.75, f=1 selected by the SMACS image-plane screen with one SPT calibration amplitude but no p/f reselection.

claim_limits: SPT selection is internal to this second cluster; only the separately reported SMACS-locked coordinate is cross-cluster.
The linearized image metric is not full nonlinear root finding.
The same singular-value regularization is retained without tuning.
One overall amplitude is calibrated and absolute gravity strength remains unpredicted.
The preferred published lens model contains a cluster halo, member halos, and three individually optimized galaxy halos.
